subject: Stratified SCR model: getting NA and -Inf logProb

messages.author: 0549e8f4a843b6d4
messages.subject: Stratified SCR model: getting NA and -Inf logProb
parts:
Hi again everyone,

I am afraid that my questions/problems may go beyond what people have time to deal with on this forum, but I am stuck and have no-one else to turn to for help, so here it is...

I am trying to adapt a code from Royle & Converse 2014 (https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/2041-210X.12135). Dr Sarah Converse's team kindly provided a functional adaptation of the original code for Nimble, and that's what I have been working with, to adapt to my study.

In my study, in Cambodia, I have 9 sites, each with 3 distinct zones along a deforestation gradient (intact, degraded, converted). each site/zone were sampled with a 50-trap grid operated for 8 consecutive nights. We repeated sampling in rainy and dry season (so 9*3*2=54 groups total). I am trying to look at change in rodent density (all species mixed, for now) according to zone and season.

 

I stayed pretty close to the original code, but some of the significant changes I made (and that are sources of potential errors) are 1) used an interaction term between season and zone effects 2) adjusted the code so the distances are calculated for the appropriate grid coordinate and trap availability, each based on 3d arrays (the original code assumed all trap grids were the same)... and I centered the coordinates on 0 so I could keep the centroid priors within the same range.

 

Attaching the code here.

 

My problem: I am getting many many rows of this as the model runs:

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[973, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[973, 2]: logProb is NA or NaN.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[973, 3]: logProb is NA or NaN.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[973, 4]: logProb is NA or NaN.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[973, 6]: logProb is -Inf.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[973, 7]: logProb is -Inf.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[973, 8]: logProb is -Inf.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[974, 1]: logProb is NA or NaN.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[974, 2]: logProb is NA or NaN.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[974, 4]: logProb is NA or NaN.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[974, 5]: logProb is NA or NaN.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[974, 7]: logProb is NA or NaN.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[974, 8]: logProb is NA or NaN.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[976, 1]: logProb is -Inf.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[976, 2]: logProb is -Inf.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[976, 4]: logProb is NA or NaN.

warning: logProb of data node Ycat[976, 8]: logProb is NA or NaN.

 

seems to affect particularly occasions for which the individual was not captured, but not all of them. It only concerns the actual individuals (n=976; not the data-augmented ones).

 

In the model outputs, al my G.N. (group-specific abundance) are the same as the data, with sd=0.

 

I have looked at the model for many hours and cannot figure out what is wrong, so calling for help. Let me know if you need anything else to help assess what's going on. I can also send data off-list.

 

Thanks

Mathieu

parts:
Mathieu, thanks for emailing the users list.  I hope we can help resolve this quandary.  That said, speaking at least for myself, I don't think I can spot the issue without being able to reproduce the error myself.  I know you mentioned that sharing data publicly is not a good option, so maybe you could send it off list, or an alternative would be sharing a set of proxy data, which you could distribute, which also replicates the error.  Either way would work.

Anyway, I hope we can figure it out, but being able to reproduce the error is paramount to the investigation.

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: Stratified SCR model: getting NA and -Inf logProb
parts: To follow-up on the NIMBLE users list, I was able to correspond with Mathieu off-list, and we identified a few minor issues in his model, which we were able to fix.  These issues amounted to borderline values being used as initial values, which gave log-probabilities of -Inf, and more subtly, numerical issues arising from inappropriate choices of initial values for several model parameters, leading to numerical underflow, and therefore probabilities identically equal to 0.  Mathieu and I were able to work through these problems, and get his model running.

Mathieu, thanks for emailing the users list.  I hope we can help resolve this quandary.  That said, speaking at least for myself, I don't think I can spot the issue without being able to reproduce the error myself.  I know you mentioned that sharing data publicly is not a good option, so maybe you could send it off list, or an alternative would be sharing a set of proxy data, which you could distribute, which also replicates the error.  Either way would work.
